lens: Accessible interaction — first encounter; simulated AI review
reason: The public first encounter is coherent and legible in the supplied desktop/mobile hero captures. Its proposition identifies student consulting and distinct client/student actions; source retains pending client approval rather than inventing outcomes, and applicant review copy accurately discloses original-resume access. I traced the client services → inquiry journey through actual source and the passing synthetic browser test. Native controls, associated application errors, visible focus treatment, generous public targets and reduced-motion handling are substantial strengths. However, operator keyboard handling can invoke a consequential result action from unrelated focused controls, and the discussion deck deliberately ignores reduced-motion preferences. Those concrete accessibility defects prevent world-class agreement and justify holding release for correction. This is independent AI source/capture assessment, not observed user success or accessibility certification.
inspected: src/app/apply/application-form.tsx (validation, recovery, navigation and rendered steps)

findings.evidence: The window keydown handler at lines 234–246 excludes only INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT and calls reveal() on every other Enter. Native By score/A to Z buttons and Exit link exist at 279–282; reveal() at 214–231 starts a drumroll and can call APPLY_STAGE_HASH. Thus Enter on an unrelated focused button/link also reaches the result shortcut.
findings.userImpact: A keyboard operator can unintentionally apply a room result while intending to sort or exit; native activation and the global shortcut compete.
findings.suggestedFix: Ignore shortcuts from interactive/contenteditable targets and handled/modifier events. Provide a native Reveal result button. Add focused-button/link Enter regressions asserting no result write.

findings.evidence: Lines 574–581 explicitly exclude .deck-root and descendants from reduced-motion overrides. Lines 522–566 define fly/spin/swoosh, shaking, confetti and infinite pulse/shimmer; deliberation-deck.tsx lines 275, 311–328, 348 and 436–439 apply them.
findings.userImpact: Motion-sensitive operators and viewers receive large movement and repeated animation despite requesting reduced motion. Projector use does not remove that access need.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the deck in reduced-motion overrides, replace motion with immediate static state changes, and verify its computed animation/transition behavior under reduced motion.

notVerified: No staging, hosted integration or human study exists. Clerk/session expiry, real Supabase/RLS/storage and actual inquiry email delivery remain unverified; the contact test intercepts HTTP success.

No live browser or full suite was run for this seat. Supplied logs show 76 passing checks; public menu focus and instrument reduced motion are sampled checks, not complete keyboard or assistive-technology coverage.

No screen-reader, physical-touch-device, Safari/Firefox, zoom/reflow or forced-colors observation. Private screens were source-reviewed; supplied hero captures do not establish their visual or task accessibility.
